Seems to be the same scribe and type of document as Moss. VIII,141.1; likely an indirect join. 

On

Verso: Autograph order in the hand of Avraham Maimonides (r. 1205–1237 CE). The cantor (Abū l-Majd?) is to give Ṭāhir the beadle (al-khādim) 2.5 dirhams. 

T-S K25.240 consists of small written orders, partly in Hebrew and partly in Arabic script, for monthly payments, made out of the rent-revenue from the pious foundation (waqf) 'Compound of the Poor' or from the pious foundation made by the physician al-Muhadhdhab. All dated orders are from spring and summer, 1218. (Information from Mediterranean Society, II, pp. 420-421, App. A 48-92; pp. 449-450, App. B 39b [dated 1210-1225]; Cohen, Pove

Recto: Document in Arabic script. Only the beginnings of eight lines are preserved. Mentions names like Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdallāh and Abū Ṭālib ʿUmar(?) b. al-Ḥasan(?), which makes it seem like a legal document.

Part of a ketubba for an unnamed bride and groom from Qalyūb. Date and names of witnesses are not preserved. The last 3 lines are in Judaeo-Arabic. Goitein (1978:127, 390, 410, 454) dates it to the 13th century, perhaps on the basis of the menstrual purity clause. (Information from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)
Accounts in Arabic script, might be fiscal. Needs examination.
Letter in the hand of Yefet b. Menashshe. In Judaeo-Arabic. Fragment (lower right corner). Mentions: ʿūd rīḥ; 3 dinars and a rubāʿī; Abū l-Ḥasan b. Hiba(?); ghārīqūn.

Official letter from the office of one of the later Maimonidean Nagids. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: between the late 13th and 1355 CE. Instructing the beadle Sulaymān to urgently summon to court a woman who had refused to accompany her husband Ṣadaqa Ibn al-Rofeʾ the previous week when he came to the court to complain about her. (Information from Mediterranean Society, III, pp. 178, 464, and from Oded Zinger's forthcoming edition.)
Magical fragment in Arabic script.
Legal document in Arabic script. Very difficult to read. On recto there is poetry in a mixture of Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic.

tags: Karaites, illness: metaphor, prison, communal strife, Ramla, catastrophes, Shelomo b. Yehuda
desc:
Letter from Ramla, from Shelomo b. Yehuda, gaʾon of the Jerusalem yeshiva, in Ramla, to his son Avraham in Fustat. Dating: 21 Iyyar 4789 (Wednesday, 7 May 1029; Gil, based on the mention of 20 Iyyar as a Tuesday, which limits the options to 1029, 1036 and 1043; Gil chooses 1029 on internal grounds). Describing in great detail the economic and other calamities that haunted Palestine in this period. 

Shelomo b. Yehuda has come down from Jerusalem to Ramla at the community's request and finds himself entangled in conflict among them, labor that requires delicacy but provides no reward. He repo
Small fragment of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Addressed to multiple people. The sender hopes to see the addressees in the place where he is traveling to. (Information in part from CUDL)
Recto: Prognostications in Arabic script. The first section is headed with an Arabic alif and a Hebrew alef in a box "اא" and the second section is headed with a Hebrew bet in a box.

Unidentified document(s) in Arabic script. Recto mentions Aḥmad b. [...] al-Khawlī(?) . . . . wa-l-nawwātiyya (something to do with the sailors?). This is then followed by the first line of a letter. Needs examination.
Accounts, including commodities (such as oil and meat) and prices, some in dinars. (Information from CUDL.) Hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef.

Letter in Arabic script. Approximately 6 lines are preserved from each side. The content is obscure. Verso is the front of the letter, and recto is the back. The front *might* contain medical advice, but it is hard to read any complete phrase or sentence. Refers to cleanliness/hygiene and to the consistency of something; also possibly a cough and young chickens, but these are tentative. The back contains a report about the travel of someone/something 'al-wasṭāniyya.' Then concludes with greetings. Merits further examination.
Small fragment of an official document in Arabic script, maybe a petition. The beginnings of 3 lines are preserved.

Sentimental letter sent by a man to his maternal uncle reporting that he and his wife are well and healthy, but perishing from longing for the recipient and the family, and giving regards to about 25 persons. Possibly dated to the 14th century. (Information from Mediterranean Society, III, pp. 25, 26, 432)

Mercantile letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Fragment (thin vertical strip from the right side of recto). Either to or from Abū Isḥāq Avraham. The sender arrived safely somewhere. Mentions brazilwood and 10 dinars; Ibn Bʿ[...]; and Abū l-Faḍl. (Information in part from CUDL)

Top of a deed of acknowledgement (iqrār). In Arabic script. Mentions a property across from the synagogue. At least one name is preserved in the opening line [...] b. Manṣūr b. Sālim(?) al-[...]. Needs examination.
Minute fragment, probably from a letter.

Letter of appeal for charity from a Byzantine man named Mosqos (=Μόσχος). Dating: ca. 1090 CE. The scribe, also a Byzantine, has been identified by Ben Outhwaite. This scribe wrote T-S 12.237, T-S NS 325.184, T-S 13J13.16, and T-S 8J16.29.

Ketubba, nearly complete. Location: Cairo. Dated: Sunday, 10 Kislev 5583 AM = 24 November 1822 CE. Between Hayyim b. Shelomo Ḥazzāq and Esther b. Eliyyahu Zarūq, with marriage payments totaling 800 riyals. The bride's name appears to have been crossed out but upon closer review it was written over an elongated taf/ת by mistake. The bride and groom each have a child or children from previous marriages, whom both parties commit to raise in the conditions section of the ketubba.

Letter from Elazar b. Shem[uel?], unknown location, to his 'brother' Abū l-Faraj ʿImrān b. Ḥasan, in Fustat. In Judaeo-Arabic. Deals mainly with matters of correspondence—who received which letter when, someone who wrote a letter in Hebrew (characters?), whether the writer will write a letter to the Levant (he will not, until "a certain date"). The writer sends greetings (and a rebuke) to Abū l-Najm Hilāl and greetings to R. Yaʿīsh al-Kohen and his son and to all the parnasim (maybe the son is the parnas ʿEli b. Ḥayyim = ʿAllūn b. Yaʿīsh of the late 11th c?). Needs further examination

Official letter. In Judaeo-Arabic and Hebrew. The hand may be known. Wide space between the lines. Addressed to a community, and containing a recommendation (or appointment?) for the bearer ("no one is to oppose him... representing us... honor him and respect him... he is deserving of all good deeds..."). (Information in part from CUDL)

tags: DIMME, illness letter 969-1517, Illness, charity, illness: colic, Petition, illness: sukuna
desc: Recto: Letter from a certain Yūsuf who is ill. In Judaeo-Arabic, with erratic handwriting and spelling, difficult to read. He explains why he couldn't come. He says that he even loaded up his donkey and set out, but then was overtaken by sukūna (a medical term that appears in other documents but whose meaning is not entirely clear) and an attack of colic (qawlanjiyya). He feared that he wouldn't make it through the night. Unclear if or how the two letters are related to each other. (Information in part from Goitein’s index card.) ASE
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Dating: 11th or 12th century. Mentions Yosef b. Yehuda and Yaḥyā and al-Mahdiyya.

Recto: liturgical text in Hebrew, with a colophon in Judaeo-Arabic by the copyist Saʿadya b. Ṣedaqa concerning the owner of the scroll, Yosef b. Moshe. Verso: one word in Hebrew (ha-rav), and a single line in Arabic (‘the rent to the end of the month of Muḥarram’). (Information from CUDL.)
A damaged bill of divorce (get). The woman’s name is Sitt al-Sada. Only the last two digits of the year is preserved: [..]82.  AA
Fragment of the siddur (prayerbook) of R. Natan al-Sijilmāsī. Shows evidence of having been preserved in a book binding (?)

Tax receipt, or possibly credit instrument? Contains an ʿalāma at the upper right, maybe, and a jahbadh signature at the bottom. Also contains the glyph, and a mirror imprint of a similar document on verso.

tags: illness letter 969-1517, Illness, Babylonian Geonim, 11th c, Illness: physician, communal, Sahlan b. Avraham, Efrayim b. Shemarya
desc: Letter from Sahlān b. Avraham perhaps to Efrayim b. Shemarya. Dating: ca. 1030 CE. Written in a calligraphic hand and beautiful biblical style. Only the right side of the letter is preserved. Sahlān refers to his illness, a physician, and going to the synagogue. Information from Bareket and from Goitein's index cards. ASE.
Minute fragment, a few incomplete words, but from what is preserved we can tell it is a ketubbah, contains the dowry section and probably written by Halfon b. Menashshe Halevi. AA
IB V, 41e. Verso: Order of payment by Abū Zikrī Kohen. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Hod should give the bearer 3 ounces of lemon-rose syrup and an ounce of chewy candy (ʿaqīd).
Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Needs examination.
Series of accounts, consisting mostly of numerical sums including two notes stating the accounts are for al-mu`alim Ya`qub Shalom al-Yahudi. Dated Muharram 1233 AH which is 1817 CE. (FGP)

tags: ib-addenda, fasting, weeping, oath, women's letter, IB3
desc: Letter from Berakha, the wife of Marwān b. Zikrī/Zekharya, to her brother Avraham b. Peraḥya Mahdawī (Ben Yiju). In Judaeo-Arabic. It is unclear if this was written before or after the family's migration from North African to Sicily. She mentions taking an oath in front of her husband (presumably one of the customary oaths of asceticism on behalf of a loved one on a dangerous voyage), but the next few words are damaged and need to be deciphered. It seems that her husband was not pleased; [lam] yarḍā lī baʿali bi-dhālika wa-jawwazahū lī wa-law ashhad fī dhālika l-ṣiyām.... She goes on to descri
Letter from Avraham, son of the Gaon, to the sons of Mevasser, Fustat, perhaps 1025.

Verso (original use): Seems to be a legal document in Hebrew. Very faded. May involve Pinḥas: ועוד אמר פנחס דנן דעו רבותי וחיי . . . ݂Merits further examination.

On recto there are formulaic phrases, possibly from a letter for a woman.
Trousseau list. Written in huge letters. No numbers for the individual items, except in last line (perhaps 43 dinars). (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi. Dated: first decade of Ḥeshvan 1445 Seleucid = October 1133 CE, under the authority of Maṣliaḥ Gaʾon. Abū l-Hasan Shelomo b. Menashshe ha-Kohen gifts a new enslaved woman, Rahaj, to his wife Sitt al-Nasab bt. Abū l-Munā Yiṣḥaq after selling the enslaved woman, ʿAlam, who was part of the wife's ketubba. Signed by Ḥalfon b. Menashshe as well as Natan b. Shelomo ha-Kohen. (Information mainly from Goitein's index card and Weiss's dissertation.)

Letter from a family member to a son or brother. In Arabic script. Dating: Probably late Mamluk or early Ottoman-era (based on handwriting, format, linguistic features). Mentions al-muʿallim Ibrāhīm Ibn al-Ṣawwāf and Ismāʿīl; the addressee's mother sends her greetings and says "by the [breast?] which you nursed, don't let her die in the presence of [...]." The addressee's sister Laṭīfa has had a baby boy, and she sends her greetings. As for the letter which the addressee sent concerning Jumayʿ(?) and the ghulām of the qāḍī Shams al-Dīn, "nothing of what you said is true." The letter concludes
Part of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Only formulaic expressions of longing are preserved. (Information in part from CUDL)
Small fragment of a prescription or account for materia medica in Arabic script. Mentions small quantities of saffron and camphor.

Deed of lease. In Arabic script. Fragment (upper right corner). The lessee is named Yūsuf b. Ibrāhīm al-Sāmirī (the Samaritan). In the upper margin, there is the draft of the beginning of a Jewish legal deed (hand of Hillel b. ʿEli?). On verso there is Hebrew literary text.
Letter of business from Yosef Ḥakīm to Mikha'el Yiṣḥaq מייארה. In Judaeo-Arabic. Late. Mentions Tunis (right page, three lines from bottom).

IB VI, 26 (ח16). Deed of release. Written and signed by Ḥalfon b. Netanel ha-Levi. Location: Probably Bharuch, India. Dating: First third of Ṭevet 1445 Seleucid, which is 29 November–8 December 1133 CE. 
Isḥāq b. Makhlūf al-Nafūsī acknowledges that he received money and goods (pearls and coral) from Barakāt b. Mūsā al-Ḥalabī. Witnesses: Ḥalfon b. Netanel ha-Levi; Avraham b. Shemuel. The validation (qiyyum) is written on a piece of paper pasted on top of the original piece, and it is not signed. India Book 4 (Hebrew description below; full English to come)

tags: Krispin, Late JA, sunduq, Istanbul, de Curiel
desc: Late letter in Judaeo-Arabic addressed to Avraham Dayyan from Binyamin de Curiel and Avraham Crespin. These men are known from other fragments. Dating: probably 18th- or 19th century based on those mentioned and paleography but there is likely a damaged date in the first line with a 54[..] AM year. Only the ת 400 numeral is legible without enhanced imaging. Rashīd (Rosetta) is mentioned in line 9, Istanbul in l. 21, and possibly Venice somewhere, but these references may only be describing goods. The verso mentions a certain Yaʿaqov Portos in line 21 in connection with the port city of Damiett

Probably fragment from accounts, mentioning a raṭl of sugar candy (sukkar nabāt) and quantities of ounces of other items including chebulic myrobalan; jottings and writing exercises on verso. (Information in part from CUDL)

Official correspondence, in Arabic script, reused for a legal document on recto in the hand of Efrayim b. Shermaya. The writer states that he will send reports on a daily basis "aktub bi-l-akhbār al-mutajaddida fī kull yawm". The phrase "aḍammathu l-kitāb al-kabīr" demands examination.

Recto (secondary use): Promissory note (IOU) -- "I owe Abū ʿAlī . . . ."

Verso (original use): Very damaged letter in Arabic script.

biblical verses and a few words of other text, followed by an elegy for the Nasi David b. Yehezkiya b. David. Yehezkiya nominated exilarch around 1021, See Franklin, This Noble House, p. 16. David, his son was a poet, middle of the eleventh century. See Franklin, p. 195, no. 27; 197, no. 43.

On verso responsum concerning the possibility of reciting havdalah over bread

Will in which a woman donates a house in the Qālūs neighborhood for religious and charitable purposes with a stipulation that she will stay in an apartment she has acquired. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (ca. 1100–38). Involves a certain Aharon. (Information from Mediterranean Society, III, p. 327; see also Goitein's index card.)

Legal document written and signed by Yeḥiʾel b. Elyaqim (active 1213–33). Quite faded. It seems that al-Rayyis Abū Saʿd gives half of a house to his daughter Sitt al-Riyāsa and her husband Efrayim. One phrase reads, "I feared lest this matter become known to the Muslims." Also signed by Yeshuʿa b. Sar Shalom ha-Kohen. (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)

Recto (secondary use): Fragment of a letter from Aharon b. Efrayim. In Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. The name Aharon b. Efrayim appears in the upper margin. Mentions Kanīsat al-Shāmiyyīn; moving from one place to another; a ḥaver; Kalev ha-Kohen (there is a Kalev ha-Kohen in several 13th century documents, but this document is 11th century); and ends with the phrase 'yeshaʿ rav.'

Letter of appeal to the Nagid, Avraham Maimonides (r. 1205–1237 CE), asking for financial assistance. Written on behalf of a foreign cloth merchant (qazzāz) named Yosef, who wants to return to his family and place. The scribe is Eliyyahu b. Zekharya. AA

State report. Large and well preserved. Dated: 5 Muḥarram 592(?) AH = 10 December 1195 CE, if read correctly. Refers to a someone with the titles Khalīl Amīr al-Muʾminīn and ʿIzz al-Dīn (both typical of viziers, though the latter might be this person's specific laqab). The sender informs the addressee that he has received 6,355.5 dirhams from the latter's brother (ṣinw). He then describes how the funds are being distributed, including distributions for the pilgrims or those who have completed the Ḥajj (al-ḥājjūn) from among the scholars (al-fuqahāʾ) and the poor (al-fuqarāʾ), and how all the r
Verso (secondary use): Maimonides' autograph of Mishne Torah, Maʿase ha-Qorbanot 15:2.

Recto, with the address on verso: Letter from [...] b. [...] al-Ṣayrafī to Abū l-Ḥusayn [...] b. Mūsā. In Judaeo-Arabic. Damaged and faded. Dating: likely ca. 13th century (paleographic dating). Mentions Abū Sulaymān. Needs examination for content.
Minute fragment, probably from a top of a letter. AA
Draft of the opening sentence of a legal document, in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe or possibly Hillel b. ʿEli. Stating that Yehuda ha-Kohen came before the witnesses.
Fragment from a prayerbook headed "siddur ṣalawāt al-yaḥid mukhtaṣar" (abbreviated book of prayers for an individual).

Interesting autobiographical narrative in Hebrew, on a bifolio. Late. About studying Torah and the grades of a broker and goldsmith?. Possibly mentions "Greeks" on the verso. Needs further examination.

Excerpts: יצאתי . . . יונים דרשתי בקוביא כניס . . . סרסור עתה שבתי כי . . . . גדלתי ואכיר. מיני מסחרים . . . בנה במלאכת הזהב לא נמצא .. . . . צורף . . . . סנדלים . . . זה לי כמה שנים לא . . . מללמוד ספר כל ענין . . . כי בישיבה ישבתי . . . דיין בזה כמעט. . . . כלי קנין . . . . 

The name Yosef appears in a different hand on one of the blank pages as does the potential surname Ṣabbagh.

Recto: Fragment from the top of a legal document. Dated: 1543 Seleucid = 1232 CE. Mentioning [...] b. Elʿazar and [...] b. Moshe ha-Sar. On verso there are jottings (accounts) in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. (Information in part from CUDL)
Fragment of a writ agency. Location: Tyre. Dated: 4772 AM = 1011/12 CE.

Letter fragment: difficult to read, faded, long, in Judaeo-Arabic. The recipient is addressed as מעלתך. Legible sections include a discussion of "sarei alafim, sari asarot, and sar ha-elef" on recto, and a little bit later, "qālū raboteinu ZL, afilu..." The writer mentions "al-Rayyis." On verso he says, "As for what Sayyidnā said regarding [.....] they wait for me, I will nevertheless [? li-'umri] come, for I am right and they are not, and I have their scripts/signatures...." Toward the bottom he mentions al-sharīʿa and someone getting lashes [yuḍrab malqot]. ASE.
Genealogies (short) of various families, written in two different hands, the first around 1150 CE, the second one generation later. (Information from Goitein's index card.)
Small fragment of a letter, probably.

Letter from Umm Ṣanīʿa/Ṣanīʿihi to the mother of ʿAbd al-Raḥīm. Fragmentary (upper right corner). In Judaeo-Arabic with some Hebrew, in a square book hand. Dating: Possibly ~13th century, based on the position of the sender's name. Approximately 10 lines of the formulaic opening are preserved, but none of the body of the message.

Fiscal document with multiple sections; conjoined tax receipts that have either been glued together or not yet cut apart. The lower fragment has registrations above it e.g. "yuthbat bi-dīwān al-ishrāf." Payment of 34 dinars? Needs further examination.

Verso is a table of Greek/Coptic numerals, which may or may not be related.
State document that begins "waṣala ilā bayt al-māl al-maʿmūr."

Fragment of deed of sale in Hebrew in which Esther bat Yosef b. Shalom, her husband Yosef, David b. Sahlan and Dosa sell to each other parts of two buildings in Fustat. The buildings are described in detail. Dated ca. 1000. (Information from Goitein's index cards)

Letter in Arabic script, with one phrase in Hebrew script. From the medieval India trade. Dating: likely second half of the 12th century (mentions Ibn Daghīsh, who appears ca. 1180 CE in T-S Misc.28.187). The sender is a well-connected Jewish merchant, possibly writing from Yemen. He refers to the arrival of goods from Fanṣūr (=present-day Barus in NW Sumatra); to a trader in Malabar (Malībar), to his own meeting with Abū l-Maʿālī b. Abū ʿAlī Ibn al-Amshāṭī in Shingli (شنجلي) (present-day Kodungallur), and to how Abū l-Maʿālī gave him a power of attorney to collect goods on his behalf in Aden.

Recto (secondary use): Letter of appeal for charity from Asʿad b. al-Ḥājj Ḥusām. In Arabic script. Dating: Probably Mamluk-era. He says that "I have nothing over me" and that he is "on the tiles/floor/pavement (ʿalā l-balāṭ)" and asks for the price of a mat (ḥaṣīra).

Small fragment from the beginning of a legal deed written by Halfon. b. Menashshe Halevi (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Avraham the judge b. Shabetay is mentioned. It is probably the judge of al-Minyat Zifta who was active there circa 1125 (Med. Soc. II, 47). AA

List of payments of rent on heqdesh houses collected in the presence of Efrayim b. Shemarya. Written by Yefet b. David. Dated [4]38/1046-7, in line 1. (Information from E. Bareket, Shafrir misrayim, pp. 61, 129, and from Mediterranean Society, IV, p. 373)

Fragment from the top of a legal document. In the hand of Natan b. Shemuel. Dated: Adar II 1456 Seleucid = February/March 1145 CE. In which Abū l-Makārim b. Abū l-Faraj al-Parnas and/or Nadiv b. Yeshuʿa ha-Parnas (appears in several other documents from this period) acknowledge a debt of 12 dinars owed to Abū Saʿd Saʿadya b. Menashshe al-Kohen (appears also in Moss. VII,125.1 (PGPID 2734)), to be repaid in monthly installments of 2 dinars. Likely an indirect join with AIU VII.D.64 (PGPID 30560).

tags: 16th c or later, early modern, learning
desc: Large notebook of Hebrew alphabet exercises. 11 folios. Dating is 16th-century or later based on the paleography and prelined paper. The name Elyaqim Dayyan and the date 27 Sivan appear on the back of the first page.

Business accounts in Judaeo-Arabic, mentioning well-known 11th-century merchants such as Mūsā b. Abū l-Ḥayy and announcing the writer's arrival in al-Mahdiyya (this part makes it seem like a note addressed to somebody else, with accounts enclosed). Also mentions al-Andalus. Commodities mentioned include flax, wax/candles, and garments such as shuqqas, fūṭas, and malḥafas. Other names mentioned: Yehuda al-Dimashqī, Abū l-Faraj, Abū l-Ḥasan, and maybe Azhar al-Kabīr. (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)
Minute fragment with some items and prices or amounts. Might connect with T-S AS 215.112 (PGPID 22876).
Recto: letter, dated [.]3 of Kislev. Mentions ʿImrān and Musāfir. Dating: probably 11th century. Verso: part of the address, including [Nahray? b. Ni]ssim ZL. (Information in part from CUDL)

Official document. Likely torn from the corner of a larger document. Dating: Ottoman-era. Contains the signature "I am the poor one Niʿmatallāh b. ʿUthmān," possibly then referring to the court of the Jāmiʿ al-Ṣāliḥ. Underneath there is an almond-shaped seal imprint featuring names such as [...] b. ʿUthman and [...] b. Sulaymān. (Information in part from FGP.)
Letter (fragment) containing greetings and copious praises for Shemuʾel Rosh ha-Seder. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Account in Judaeo-Arabic. Small fragment. Mentions watermelon, soap (ghasūl), and sums of money.
Letter fragment. Refers to the arrival of a raqqāṣ (runner/courier) in search of the sender (ʿabduhā).

Letter from Hilāl b. Avraham, in Alexandria(?), to his brother Abū Naṣr b. Avraham, in Fustat(?). The sender is worried about Abū l-Karam whose only desire is to 'sue for the 100 dinars' (or conceivably 'sue the dead man for a dinar,' but this seems less likely). Hilāl hardly finds the energy to keep on opening his shop any more. He passes on news of various people and then writes about an unspecified matter, "For the matter requested from you by me you must be desirous of toil, prepared to take heavy loads upon your back and prove that you are worthy of your renown; do not fancy that what can

Recto: collection of notes on astral medicine, connecting the human body, physiognomy, hair colour and various bodily functions to the rising of a particular star. The fragment is possibly a draft or part of a booklet for personal use. Verso: Hebrew alphabetical exercises. (Information from CUDL.)
Recto: Legal fragment (or formulary or draft?). In Judaeo-Arabic. The larger text block contains phrases of release (ibrāʾ) possibly on the termination of a partnership. Needs further examination.
Magical text, mentioning ‘the people of Babel’ (ahl Bābil) and the Neguš. Magical drawing on verso. Looks like the same hand as T-S AS 145.71 + T-S Ar.30.81 (=Abū Sahl Levi?).
Accounts in Arabic script. Large, filling four columns. Consists entirely of columns of names with eastern Arabic numerals.
Possibly a fiscal document in Arabic script. Very stylized. One entry begins: "al-maḍmūn..."

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Damaged and faded. Dating: likely ca. 13th century or later (based on handwriting, names, and linguistic features). Greetings to ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and his brother Naṣrallāh. The addressee is urged to come quickly.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and eastern Arabic numerals. Very dense. Many names appear. One of the pages is dated Parshat Vayigash 5563 AM = 1802 CE.

Deed about paying a debt in installments, probably by a husband (Meshullam, known as Abu al-Makarim) to his wife (Sitt al-Baha bt. Yehuda). The document likely includes the condition that if the husband were to claim that he has paid without it being written on the back of the deed or corroborated by two witnesses, his claim would be void. (Oded Zinger, Women, Gender and Law: Marital disputes according to documents of the Cairo Geniza, 150-1) EMS
Deed of lease (istiʾjar). An Iqrār. In Arabic. Mentions a date in the body of the text: 12 Dhū l-Qaʿda 531 AH = 1 August 1137 CE. Also mentions safātij. Needs further examination.
Address of a letter sent to al-Maḥalla, to Abū l-M[...].
Few words from the end of a legal document
Record of an monetary transaction involving Abū Al-Faraj al-Dimyati (who might be Nethanel Halevi, Halfon's father) , and mentioning bread (recto); Arabic letter (? needs examination)
Beginning of a court record dated Shevat 1411/ February 1100. On parchment. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Legal document. In the hand of Hillel b. ʿEli? Dated: 15 Ḥeshvan 1410 Seleucid, which is 1098 CE. Involves [...] bt. Nissim and her ex-husband M[...]. (Information in part from CUDL)
Accounts of some sort. In Arabic script. Dated: Ṣafar 518 AH = March/April 1124 CE.

tags: Nahray B. Nissim, al-Tahirti, flax, trade
desc:
Fragment of a business letter from Barhun b. Salih al-Tāhartī in Busir, probably to Nahray b. Nissim in Fustat, mentioning bales of flax being prepared for shipment to Alexandria and places further on, and the writer's intention to travel to Mahdiyya. Dated ca. 1046. (Information from Gil)
Description from PGPID 5823:
Letter from Barhun b. Salih al-Tāhartī, from Busir, probably to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat. Around 1046. The writer sold goods in the Delta area and arranged flax shipments from Alexandria. He is planning to travel to Mahdiyya. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 3, #330) VMR

Letter from Sulaymān to his brother Abū l-Manṣūr. In Judaeo-Arabic. Opens with a blistering rebuke for the lack of letters and the failure to inquire about the writer whether with Jews or with Muslims, then "what I want from you now is for you to 'wash your face with me' by treating the bearer of this letter well." There follow instructions about various business matters, including materia medica (ḥawā'ij ʿiṭr). Mentions Abū Naṣr Ibn Khalaf. Mentions an agency (wakāla). Mentions silk. Asks for two qinṭārs of marble from the maghā'ir (caves?). Greetings to many people, including the parents of
Opening of a ketubba for Malka bat Yeshuʿa (bride) in a very calligraphic script. Reference to 20 dinars. There are many pen trials in the top margin and on verso. (Information from CUDL.)

tags: illness: travel, Illness: women's, epidemic, Illness, illness: dying, personal, illness: gastrointestinal
desc: Recto: Letter from (or written on behalf of) a woman to her son Avraham ('Rabbenu'). In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Probably no earlier than 14th century, and conceivably much later, based on script and vocabulary. Mentions an area called ḥawsh al-maghāriba in Fustat, where Avraham's sister lives. The letter contains cryptic exhortations about associating with Gentiles, directed at Avraham as well as a certain Raḥel (his wife?). The letter also informs him that his sister's daughter Ḥabība is "stricken" (maḍrūba) and is on the verge of death. "Every day brides and grooms go forth from the neighborh

Letter in Ladino, sent by Isaac Baronito to his father Abraham Baronito, Mitzrayim. (Information from CUDL.) Isaac addresses his father as "the crown of my head" (la corona de mi cabeza). It concerns books with "glosses in his hand": sabreis komo he hallado ke tienen los libros haga'ot eskeritura de su mano y me recelo y si kereis aun kon todo esto ke os los envie os los enviare mas ha de saver ke no los vendas a ningun modo por amor de la dicha ke tiene ... y si keres os man dare los libros komo kedamos haya de ser kon este partido ke no los haveis de vender a ningun por la razon. Information

Bill submitted to Avraham Maimonides: the cantor 'al-Makīn' is owed 9 dirhams for 6 weeks, and Abū l-Ṭāhir is owed 1.5 dirhams for 3 weeks. Avraham Maimonides then wrote "the total: 7.5" and on verso "let it be paid from the rent of the compound." All this is on a reused scrap from an earlier Arabic-script document.

T-S K25.240 consists of small written orders, partly in Hebrew and partly in Arabic script, for monthly payments, made out of the rent-revenue from the pious foundation (waqf) 'Compound of the Poor' or from the pious foundation made by the physician al-Muhadhdhab. All dated orde
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals, mentioning al-Maḥallī, loans from Ibrāhīm and Bū l-Maʿānī, trash collection, a carpenter, an apartment.
Many pages (~20) of a Ladino literary work. It seems to be historical in nature, set in the time of Shimʿon b. Sheṭaḥ.

Legal document; Literary text.
Recto: paraphrase of sections of Esther with biblical phrases in Hebrew (including Esther 8:8; 3:13); Coptic numerals. Verso: further paraphrase of Esther; tajriba in Judaeo-Arabic (from CUDL). The hand of the literary piece and the tajriba is by a known scribe, Yosef b. Shemuʾel Halevi (ca. 1180's-1210). 
Also on verso, on the right side of the page, a bottom part from a legal deed from Tishrei 1511 (1199) by a different hand. 
Hebrew, Judeo-Arabic, Coptic numerals. AA

Letter sent from Qayrawān by Yosef b. Khalfa to Khalluf b. Faraḥ b. al-Zarbī, probably in Fustat dealing with goods and their prices in Palermo. Dating: ca. 1030 (Goitein) or ca. 1050 (Gil) or uncertain (Ben-Sasson).
Accounts.

Simha, daughter of Moshe b. Job, wife of Yosef al-Bali, sells a Pentateuch with gilded ornaments to Yiṣḥaq b. Avraham. Dated Iyyar 5159/April-May 1399. (Information from Goitein's index cards and from a note on the typed text)

Verso and top margin of recto: Accounts dealing mainly with clothing items and women's names, mostly Muslim names. Also several men identified by their mother's names, which is very unusual outside of magic and prayers. A distribution list related in some way to the petition? Items named include ṢMT (צמת), radda, and fūṭa, and quantities (of cloth?) in cubits (דראע). Names include "Ghālib b. Sitt al-Ahl" "from Abū l-Faḍl b. Fāṭima" (recto top margin). On verso: "the woman wearing the radda"; "the one known as Sitt al-ʿAlam"; Fāṭima bt. Farjiyya the old woman (al-ʿajuz); [...] bt. al-Jayyida; M

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. This portion preserves only a long, elaborate introduction and a few words of the body. There is an ان شا الله written in Arabic script in the midst of the Hebrew script. On verso there is Hebrew literary text.
Deuteronomy 34:3-12, with a colophon in Judaeo-Arabic dated 1665 Sel. (= 1353/54 CE). (Information from CUDL.)
Copy of a letter of appeal for charity. In Hebrew. In exquisite script and high style. Addressed to Pinḥas b. Peʾer ha-Qehillot. (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Marriage contract (ketubba). Dated: Tuesday, 17 Elul 16[29?] Seleucid, which would be 1318 CE. The first and final letter of the missing digits are clearly ע. Goitein suggests 1292–97 CE, but that does not seem possible. Under the reshut of the Nagid Avraham b. David (Avraham II) Maimonides. If indeed this is from 1318 CE, it might be the latest known mention of Avraham II as Nagid. Groom: Shemuel b. Shela ha-Talmid. Bride: Muwaffaqa bt. Yeshuʿa, a widow. No dowry mentioned. 5+20=25. Information in part from Goitein's index card.

Upper part of a long vertical letter. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: probably 12th or 13th century. Addressed to a notable. Reporting something about Furayj al-Bayyāʿ; couriers; shops; some people demanding 10 pounds of something; 2 dirhams and a chicken; shopkeepers closing their shops (going on strike?); the phrase "if the elder sent even the littlest boy (or: the most insignificant person) requesting our children, we would bring them to him"; someone not eating cheese; and the couriers again. The continuation is missing and most of the context is unclear.
Ketubba fragment. Groom: Ḥalfon b. ʿEli. Bride: Zayn, a virgin. See Goitein's index card.

Order of payment relating to communal administration. The addressee is supposed to settle accounts with Sālim and Maḥfūẓ 'the collectors' (jābīs) for the 20 dirhams which they paid to the nāʾib, including by paying them 2 dirhams by way of brokerage (juʿl). Dating: 12th or 13th century.
Memorial lists, mentioning Netanʾel ha-Levi and [Abū] l-Ḥasan Ibn al-Fāḍil b. [...]. Mainly in Hebrew, with some Arabic (in Arabic script) interspersed. (Information mainly from CUDL)

Ketubba. Location: Fustat. Dated: Thursday, 5 Ḥeshvan 1553 Seleucid = 11 October 1241 CE, without any reshut clause. Bride: a widow called 'al-Sitt al-Fāḍila' bt. Shela. Groom: Yeḥezqel b. Eliyya. Goitein notes "In Aramaic; despite the bad preservation worth studying for the Aramaic formulary.) (Information from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)
Prayer for the community at the time of a plague, and memorial list of persons who had died in it, including an unmarried girl. (Information from Goitein's index card.)
Document in Judaeo-Arabic, small fragment. Mentions a thawb ʿattābī and some prices in dirhams. Looks like the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi.
Small fragment from a letter written by Yefet b. Menashshe Halevi

Letter describing a sea voyage from Tripoli to Sicily (CUDL). “Of another Jew we read in a Hebrew letter that in a large ship, in which thirty-six or -seven Jews and about three hundred Muslims traveled, he was 'the treasurer and commander' (probably fixing the fares and deciding where the goods of the merchants should be stowed). Like Makhlūf, this 'treasurer' was a scholarly person and used the time before the departure of the boat to study with the writer of that Hebrew letter, a rabbi from Christian Europe.” (Goitein, Med. Soc. x, B, 2, 139.) Bibliography: Assaf, Texts, 133.

tags: Yisrael b. Natan, Byzantine merchants, Byzantines, trade
desc: Letter from Barhūn b. Mūsā al-Tāhartī, probably from Alexandria, to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat. Dating: ca. 1062 (Gil). Barhūn is writing also in the name of his brother, Yosef. He has been in Sfax and al-Mahdiyya. He mentions large shipments of dirhams and several of Nahray’s other business partners. Deals with selling and shipping goods to al-Mahdiyya, Tripoli, and Sicily and prices. Also mentions Rūm who want peppe. Mentions some family matters about Nahray’s maternal aunt who is in a bad financial situation, and his cousin Yisra'el b. Natan, who is in mental distress (or is simply engaged in
Biblical (book of Numbers). Yemeni hand? On verso there is a pen trial: tajribat qalam wa-ḥibr malīḥ ṭāʾil.

Legal deed. Location: Fustat/Cairo. Dated: Tuesday, 2 Elul 5319 AM, which is 1559 CE. In which Yiṣḥaq Luria Ashkenazi (the famous kabbalist) sells 8 1/3 kikars of pepper from his stock in Alexandria to Natan Ḥefeṣ for a sum of 150 Venetian peraḥim. The pepper is to be given to Reuven Bavli, evidently Natan's agent. Information from FGP.
Six lines of poetry or rhymed prose in Arabic script, with wide line spacing. Probably the introduction to a formal (state?) letter. Reused for Hebrew piyyuṭ on verso.
Letter, probably. In Judaeo-Arabic. Extremely faded.
Several of the psalms in Judaeo-Arabic (לא לנו... אהבתי כי ישמע...). 19th century. The paper has red vertical lines, including one squiggly line.

Beginning of a circular letter by Nisi b. Shemuel, head of a congregation (of Rabbanites? Palestinians? Babylonians? Karaites?) to all Israel, emphasizing the duty to act like zealots of the type of Phineas and Eliyyahu in religious matters. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Minute fragment. recommend suppress

Fragment of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic, maybe mercantile. Mentions Sar ha-Sarim; a burniyya (a kind of vessel); 'our master' (adonenu); a paste (maʿjūn); Ibrāhīm al-[...]; and a small amount of ambergris (ʿanbar). Resembles the handwriting of Hillel b. ʿEli in the letters he wrote for Yosef Lebdi (see India Book I), but does not appear to be a direct join with any of them.

Bill of divorce (geṭ). Location: Cairo. Dated: 29 Tevet 1443 Seleucid, which is 19 January 1132 CE. Husband: Yeshuʿa b. ʿEli. Wife: Sitt al-Fakhr bt. Ṣedaqa. The witnesses are Natan b. Shelomo ha-Kohen and Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi. The verso contains the acceptance of the bill of divorce by the wife, signed by the witnesses Yosef b. Yefet ha-Levi and Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi. (Information from Goitein's index card and CUDL.)
Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals.
Small fragment from the top of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. The address is partially preserved, including the name Abū l-[...] [...] b. Hillel al-Dimashqī.
Magical fragment in Arabic script. It seems "throbbing of the joints" (ḍarabān al-mafāṣil).

Accounts of a slaughterer. In Judaeo-Arabic. He receives 1 dirham for 2 heads (probably of sheep). First week of Elul: 43 heads, 22 dirhams. Second week: 24 dirhams. Third week: 23.75 dirhams. Fourth week: 24.5 dirhams. He then lists numerous goods that he purchased in Cairo (including fruit, and a payment for winemaking). (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Fragment of a letter from Nehemya ha-Kohen, the Pumbedita Gaon, to one of the members of the Babylonian community in Fustat, probably the beginning of 963. As in Bodl. MS heb. b 12/25 (PGPID 5591), polemicizes against "Kaḥshon" (Naḥshon) and "Shevira" (the future Gaʾon Sherira b. Ḥananya). Asks to renew the connections between them by a gaon’s emissary, probably Shlomo b. ʿEli b. Ṭavnay, and by Ṭuv Aluf and the sons of Aharon ha-Baghdadi. Reused on verso for accounts in Arabic script resembling those in T-S 12.851 (PGPID 38160). (Gil, Kingdom, vol. 2, #17.) VMR
A few words from the end of a decree: واعـ[ـلم هذا] واعمل عليه وبحسبه وو . . . . Reused for Hebrew liturgy.
Small fragment of a ketubba. The numbers 15 and 40 appear. The names Yefet and Sitt al-[...] may appear in the bottom line.

On verso there is a neat table of all the Greek/Coptic numerals in ascending order from 1 to 900,000 (the symbols start repeating after a thousand -- they are the the same symbols as before but underlined).
Legal document. Dated: 1454 Seleucid = 1142/43 CE. Mentions 'the seat (moshav) of our master'; 6 dinars; a woman; and an inheritance. (Information mainly from CUDL)
Small fragment of document(s) in Arabic.
Document with list of names, either with remarks such as ‘will testify’ or with numerals, mentioning Ibn Zurayq; Abū l-Surūr Ibn al-Kohen, Khallūf and Sitt (or Bayt?) Nissim. (Information from CUDL)
Tables in Arabic script and Coptic numerals. Mainly foods and materia medica and amounts.

Verso: List of contributors or recipients of communal funds. Dating: ca. 1221 CE, based on recto. Mentions names such as Bū ʿImrān and his father; Bū l-ʿAlāʾ; al-Thiqa; al-faqī[h]; Ibn al-Shāmiyya; Sayyidnā; R. Ḥananʾel; loans for Ibn ʿIwāḍ and Bū ʿAlī Ibn al-Munajjā; Bū Manṣūr b. Baqāʾ; Ibn al-ʿAfīf; Bū l-Faḍl; and al-Makīn. On recto also mentions R. Yeḥiʾel.
Verso: Very faded accounts in Arabic and Coptic numerals. Recto is piyyuṭ.
Qurʾan. Last pages of the Qurʾan. See T-S Ar.38.8. (Information from Goitein’s index card)

tags: tax, communal, capitation tax, bialphabetic, Appeal
desc: Letter in Arabic script. The sender is a man from Alexandria who was forced to flee from that city because he was unable to pay the capitation tax for his little boy. He asks the Nagid Avraham Maimonides to instruct the judge Eliyyahu to help. He had been unsuccessful in obtaining work. See verso.

Accounts or reckoning, mentioning names such as Muḥammad and Ḥusayn. Dating: probably Ottoman-era given the reference to a certain Mūṣlū Çorbacı in the lower entries on the verso (possibly an Ottoman military officer). The name below that probably includes a misspelling of the Ottoman military rank katkhūda (Tr. kethüda): daughter of Muṣṭafa Kadkhūda, בת מוצטפה כדכודה.(ASE/MCE with information from CUDL)

Letter from Avraham b. Ṣedaqa, in Ashqelon, to Abū Saʿīd Netanʾel b. Ṣedaqa al-ʿAṭṭār, in Fustat. In Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic, with the address in Arabic script. Dated: Elul 1427 Seleucid = August/September 1116 CE. Apart from the opening blessings, consists mainly of a request that the addressee pay 5 dinars to the sender's relative Abū l-Ḥasan Rajāʾ of Ashqelon. Cf. CUL Or.1080 J127 (PGPID 8896).

tags: Abu l-Hasan b. Wahb, daman, tax, damin
desc: Receipt issued to the khuzzān of the Fayyūm tax districts against revenue delivered by Abū l-Ḥasan b. Wahb. Amount: one-quarter, one-sixth and two ḥabbas (Khan read one-eighth, two qīrāṭs and one). Dated: 24 Muḥarram 404. Written by the jahbadh Mīkhāʾīl b. ʿAbd al-Masīḥ. Measurements: 12.5 × 7.7 cm. The verso is blank.
Recto: Short genealogical list of the Ghuzūlī family and another family.

Letter addressed to [Na]tan ha-Kohen ha-Ḥaver (=Natan b. Shelomo?). In Judaeo-Arabic. Only pieces of the first few lines and 7 lines in the upper margin are preserved. The upper margin mentions M. Menashshe and M. Yeshuʿa and a poor man named Yūsuf and a dinar.

Power of attorney (שטר אורכתא). Mentions: Makhlūf Ibn ʿAyn Sārra; Yiṣḥaq [ha-Le]vi b. [...] al-ʿAjamī; Alexandria; 6 dinars; Moshe Neʾeman ha-Yeshiva (he may be the agent for obtaining the 6 dinars from somebody else). The physician (ha-rofeʾ) ʿOvadya b. Yefet ha-Levi is the person issuing the power of attorney. Date and location are not preserved. Makhlūf Ibn ʿAyn Sārra is known from numerous documents from the India trade spanning the period 1103 (T-S 12.392) to 1141 (ENA 4020.8)—see Goitein, Med Soc V, p. 246f. This document is from the earlier end of that range, as it was validated by Ṣado

Verso, 90 degrees: Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. In the hand of Yosef b. Yaʿaqov Rosh ha-Seder. Mentioning several scribes and skins (presumably as writing surface). The remaining text is all literary - see FGP for identifications.
Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Only a few phrases are preserved, including "the deliverance of the girl" (khalāṣ al-ṣabiyya), a phrase which often refers to childbirth.
Probably opening of a letter to a notable.

Report of the death of a Jewish woman. In Arabic script. The deceased is Saʿdiyya bt. Yūsuf al-Yahūdi. Her father, Yūsuf, is the heir. Dated: Tuesday, 8 Rajab 657 AH, which is 1 July 1259 CE. Witnesses: Hibatallāh b. Faḍāʾil; Bū Saʿd b. Yūsuf b. Sālim. (Information from CUDL and Khan.)
Some Arabic jottings on verso, may be documentary.

Recto: Letter concerning an order for a cloak (mulāʾa) which the writer had sent but the addressee had not confirmed receiving. In Judaeo-Arabic. Deferential tone throughout. The sender may be named Abū l-Surūr (l. 6). He previously sent a letter with Abū Daniʾel Maḥfūẓ asking for the addressee's instructions concerning the preparation of the mulāʾa (הל תדק או תמרש פקט). He did not hear anything and so he completed both operations (וקד מרשת אלמלאה ודקתהא) and sent it with Abū l-Munā Ibn al-Dihqān. He now asks for confirmation of receipt. Greetings to 'our rabbi Moshe.' 

Verso: Accounts in A
Legal document (probably a formulary) for marriage conditions. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Much of the text resembles the text of ENA 3755.6 (PGPID 4760).

Letter from Yehuda b. Avraham b. Faraj, in Ṣahrajt (Goitein) or Jerusalem (Gil), to ʿEli b. ʿAmram (aka Abū l-Husayn ʿAllūn b. Muʿammar), in Fustat. In Hebrew and Arabic (in Arabic script). Dating: ca. 1065 CE; at any rate, under the gaonate of Eliyyahu ha-Kohen, because it ends with the motto (ʿalāma) Yeshaʿ Yuḥash. Goitein identified the sender's location as Ṣahrajt since that is where Yehuda b. Avraham drew up Bodl. MS heb. c 28/5. Gil suggests that he is Yehuda ha-Ḥazzan of Jerusalem (unclear which other documents this man is known from) and just happened to be staying in Ṣahrajt in 1060 C

Fragment of a letter/petition in Judaeo-Arabic, apparently to the Nagid. Appealing for help as well as help for a woman oppressed by her husband. Her husband intended to redeem a captive woman and take her as a second wife. (Information from Friedman.)
Small fragment of a letter: closing greetings and the phrase "send it to me with whomever..."

Some sort of multiplication table describing the results of multiplying different orders of magnitude, e.g. "the tens with the thousands, the answer is. . ." Accompanied by numerals. Verso is not digitized (CUDL and FGP only have two images of recto). 

There is also Hebrew text with a discourse on the calendar, mentioning the different types of Hebrew year (complete, normal, defective; leap, regular) and rules for calendar reckoning. (Information in part from CUDL.)

Letter sent from al-Mahdiyya (Gil)/ al-Maghrib (Ben-Sasson) to Fustat (Gil)/Sicily (Ben-Sasson), by Ishaq b. Ali al-Majjani to Abu al-Fadl, dealing with a debt of Banu al-Majjani to one named al-Shiraji (Gil) and mentioning legal opinion of Rabbi Hananel b. Hushiel and Masliah b. Eliyyahu. Dated ca. 1039 (Gil). (Information from M. Gil, Kingdom, Vol. IV, p. 109 and from M. Ben-Sasson, Yehudei sitziliya, p.116)

Legal document. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Fragment (lower right piece). Likely the will of a certain Shemuel. Mentions his cousins (banū ʿamm), his sister, and many other names including [...] b. Yehuda, Shemarya b. Y[...], Meʾir, Yaʿqūb, and Yisr[aʾel?].

Small legal or official document. Written on a small, narrow slip, with annotations in the upper margin. In some ways more resembles an order of payment. At upper left there is a witness clause: شهد على ال ؟؟؟؟ في السادس . . . . . . Needs further examination.
State document, possibly. In Arabic script in a chancery hand. A few words preserved from 2 lines, including "waḥdahu" and "al-mamlūk." On verso there is Hebrew literary text.

tags: ib-partial translation-heb, ib-untranslated-eng, India Book, IB4
desc:
IB IV, 64 (ח88). Letter from Saʿdān b. Thābit al-Baghdādī ha-Levi, in Alexandria, to Ḥalfon b. Netanel ha-Levi, in Fustat. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: ca. 1135 CE. 

Goitein identified the sender based on his handwriting (which is corroborated by the content of IV,89). Apparently, Saʿdān had sent Ḥalfon a shipment of pearls. He complains about Ḥalfon’s plan to travel to Damascus by land rather than by ship from Alexandria because Saʿdān expected them to meet there, and so Ḥalfon would pay all or part of the debt that Ḥalfon's brother Abū ʿAlī Yeḥezqel owed to Saʿdān. Ḥalfon had already describ
Lists of numerals such as 1702, 360, and quantities of dinars, such as 30 dinars and 10 dinars. (Information from CUDL)
Recto: Letter fragment from Yehuda b. Ṭoviyya ha-Kohen, in Bilbays, to Avraham Maimonides, in Fustat. Only the tarjama with Yehuda's name is preserved.

Note in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe addressed to "al-Nezer" (Natan b. Shemuʾel) asking him to send a note to Abū l-[...] instructing him to "check/investigate" [...] of "the woman" and "all of her affairs." Dating: ca. 1128–1138 based on the years when the sender (ca. 1100–1138) and recipient (ca 1128–1164) were active. (Information in part from CUDL.)

Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Might be match for one of the Spanish or Maghribī hands from India Book IV — like Ibn Ezra in H37, the writer of H52, or the scribe in the margin of JRL B 5758. Needs examination.
Muslim marriage contract. (Information from Naïm Vanthieghem.)
Small fragment of a legal deed written on parchment. Probably regarding a debt from an husband called Sahlān to his wife, but too little text is preserved. Dating: probably 11th century. AA/ASE

Large bifolio of accounts in Arabic script. Might be fiscal. On recto, sections are headed by names of profession ("the dyers (al-ṣabbāghīn)... the millers (al-ṭaḥḥānīn)..."), each with lists of names with numbers underneath. On verso, one page was reused for a Judaeo-Arabic list written at 180 degrees in a crude hand, mentioning names such as Bū l-ʿAlāʾ, Baqāʾ b. Nuʿmān (appears also in T-S Misc.8.13 (PGPID 23487)), and Ibrāhīm.
Top of a document in Arabic script, very faded/damaged.

Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Lists many names, including Abū Bishr; Abū Isḥāq; ʿArūs; Khalaf; Abū l-ṭāhir; Ibn al-ḥijāziyya; Salāma; Abū l-Munā; al-Dimyāṭī; and Musallam/Muslim Ibn al-Qābila ('son of the midwife'). Several entries are overlined. 

On verso (different hand): "our master"; Abū l-Mufaḍḍal; the son of Abū l-Surur; David; Shemarya.
Possibly a fiscal account in Arabic script, reused for a Judaeo-Arabic list of items and quantities written between the lines.
List of quantities of commodities, including 1/2 ratl of tamarind. In Judaeo-Arabic. Information from Shivtiel/Nissen catalog.

Recto: Letter of the Na'ib of Malij to the judge Efrayim b. Meshulam regarding a case of an orphan girl. Asks for a quick decision. Verso: The answer, it seems in the hand of Meir b. Hillel b. Sadoq. Further information and partial transcriptions on Goitein's note card.
Tax receipt? Very faded.

Fragment of a letter in Hebrew, containing praises for an exilarch: ונסיך . . . הוצק חן . . . אומר על ברי . . . בהזהירו זהי . . . . וזוגיו וחביריו . . . . ודורך על במתי שו . . . . נשיא גליותינו גאון תפא[רת] . . . נשיא ישראל ויהודה ראש . . . . משארית יעקב בימיו . . . . 

Verso looks like piyyuṭ.

Verso: Bill of divorce. Location: Fustat. Dated: 1564 Seleucid, which is 1252/53 CE. Husband: Nissim b. Sar Shalom ha-Levi of Damascus, the same husband from recto. This document was not completed. See also ENA 2559.15 (PGPID 11080) for another unsigned geṭ between the same couple from the preceding year.
Recto: Legal document, in Arabic script. Fragment (the right halves of ~7 lines) of a marriage contract. Mentions the mahr (dower). Needs examination.

State-document fragment concerning a disputed payment associated with cattle. The petitioners ask for the issuance of an authoritative order ensuring that they are charged only the recognised amount per head of cattle, without additional exaction or injustice. The surviving text also mentions ḍamān and khafāra, but their precise role is unclear. The document ends with a taṣliya and ḥasbala. Needs examination.

Letter addressed to Eli (‘Allun) ha-parnas, active 1057-1107, which mention his less well-known son, the parnas Abu Kathir (Efrayim ha-Kohen b. ‘Eli). (Oded Zinger, Women, Gender and Law: Marital Disputes According to Documents of the Cairo Geniza, 359) EMS
Order of payment in Arabic script. The judge (al-dayyān) is asked to pay 5 dinars to the bearer. See T-S AS 179.212 (PGPID 36725) and the related orders listed there.
Very faded letter in the hand of Yehuda b. Ṭuviyyahu ha-Kohen, who was the muqaddam of Bilbays (active 1172–1218).
Minute fragment. Only a few words are preserved. It can be a literary fragment, but also poetical Hebrew phrases from an opening of a letter to a notable. AA

Recto: (draft of a?) letter with jottings. The sender mentions "his headache" and the sender's intention to travel east (אלממלוך קד עזם קולא ואחדא עלי אלתוגה נחו אלשרק). Dating: probably ca. late 12th or early 13th century.

Verso: jottings. (Information from CUDL)

tags: Abu l-Hasan b. Wahb, tax receipt, daman, damin
desc: Tax receipt issued to Abū l-Ḥasan b. Wahb for his ḍamān on dyeing in Madīnat al-Fayyūm. Dated: 20 Shawwāl 405. Written by the jahbadh Mīkhāʾīl b. ʿAbd al-Masīḥ. Payment made under the supervision of three officials: (1) the auspicious, rightly guided qāḍī Thiqat al-Mulk Makīn al-Dawla wa-Amīnuhā, protégé of the Commander of the Faithful, Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Nahār (2) (in) the presence of the fiduciary qāḍī Abū ʿAlī l-Ḥasan b. Yaḥyā b. Nahār on his behalf, and (3) (under) the tax accounting of the elder Sadīd al-Dawla Abū l-Faraj ʿAbd al-Masīḥ b. Qūrīl. Measurements: 12.5 × 8.1 cm. The verso co
Fragment of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: ca. 12th century. Mentioning sending things with different people, including cheese. (Information in part from CUDL)

A few words from a letter in Arabic script. Large script, wide space between the lines. Reminiscent of a state document but the preserved content seems to be mercantile: "I sent it with the two of them for the sake of buying..." (aṣḥabtuhumā iyyāh bi-rasm shirā...). Reused for Hebrew piyyuṭ on recto.

Fragment of a legal document. Spanish hand. concerning monetary issues between Isḥāq b. Asher (appears also in T-S 10J13.1 (PGPID 7878)) and Khallūf al-Fāsī. Dated: Monday, [...] [4]870 AM = August/September 1110 CE. Concerning a sum of 107 dinars that must be repaid before Passover. Also mentions Latakia (לאדקיא). On recto there are business accounts with some entries cricled.

tags: India Book, collateral, IB1, Lebdi, ib-untranslated-eng
desc:
IB I, 15. Three testimonies regarding collateral deposited by Yosef al-Lebdi the India trader. Lebdi owed Ḥasan b. Bundar, the representative of the merchants in Aden, 40 dinars for an indigo deal. Until Lebdi could pay the debt in full, he had to deposit collateral, probably because he was a foreigner who was expected to leave town. The first and last of these three entries are written and signed by Netan’el b. Yefet.
The first is signed by Netanel, Yiṣḥaq b. Shemu'el and Eli ha-Kohen b. Yaḥya. The last is signed by Netanel and Yiṣḥaq b. Shemu'el.
This is the recto of the second leaf of CUL
Poetry, probably. In Judaeo-Arabic. There is also alphabet practice and numbers in western Arabic numerals (so the date is relatively late).

Letter in the hand of Avraham Maimonides in which he instructs Fakhr al-Dawla regarding a sum of money, nine dinars, still owed, and what to tell Abu al-'Ala about it. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Order of commodities in Judaeo-Arabic, maybe related to the India trade. Mentions various items measured in cubits and four brass springs (? lawālib).
Recto: Letter fragment in Arabic script. "... that it is correct. As for... that it is correct. And when..."
Horoscopes. In Judaeo-Arabic.

Late letter in Judaeo-Arabic (dated, but confusingly) to Ḥayyim ha-Kohen and Ḥayyim Ṭaliṭ(?) or Shlīsh. The date makes use of 1000 symbol V to indicate the millennium: Vה = five thousand. Oddly, the letter sender then appears to combine ת (400) with the western Arabic numeral 5, yielding a potential reading of 6 Shevat 5405 AM. The corresponding year 1645 CE does not seem very likely given the paleography and high degree of paper preservation, therefore, the ligature before 5 should also be considered as ק– possibly another multiple: ק5 = five hundred. The year 1745 CE seems more likely, but t

Recto: Letter fragment addressed to a notable, in Hebrew. 

Verso: Remnant of an official letter or document in Arabic script. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Fragment of a legal document, mentioning the name [...]el al-Lādiqī. (Information from CUDL)
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic ("qāʾima mubāraka..."). Dated: Muḥarram 957 AH = 1550 CE. Mentions the term jāmakiyya.
Minute fragment. Damaged. Probably a list or accounts, mentioning names, such as Isḥaq. (Information from CUDL)
A few letters are preserved from an Arabic state document, probably a decree. Reused for Hebrew piyyuṭ.

Fatimid state document. May be headed "al-ʿimāra." The term "mablagh" may appear in the second long line. Needs examination. Reused by the same Hebrew scribe who reused many Arabic documents from the time of al-Afḍal.
Trousseau list. Groom: Ghālib b. Faraj. Bride: Sara bt. Avraham.

Brief business letter from Nissim b. Hillel to Ibrāhīm b. Maḥfūẓ (=Avraham b. Shemarya? Or maybe the first name is Efrayim instead of Ibrāhīm). In Arabic script. Faded. Dating: Probably 11th century. Needs examination for content. Mentions Jerusalem in l. 4. Needs further examination.

Original use: remnant of a state document (fiscal register?). Very little is preserved apart from a date: the end of Dhū l-Ḥijja 546(?) AH, which would be April 1152 CE if read correctly. Reused for a responsum on the superiority of Aaron over David, quoting biblical sources (Numbers 18:11; Malachi 2:5; Numbers 17:11; 2 Chronicles 23:13). (Information in part from CUDL.)

Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Detailed, with many names of people and goods. Mentions: the ṣināʿa; Hārūn al-Kohen who agrees on a payment plan; Abū l-ʿAlāʾ, whose warehouse is mentioned several times; Ibn al-Raṣṣāṣiyya; the term juwārīsh (stomachic); lemon; al-Ḥuṣrī; kerchiefs.

Hand of Abū Zikrī Kohen?

Letter from Simḥa ha-Kohen, in Alexandria, to Abu ʿImrān Moshe "The Pride of the Priests" (Tifʾeret ha-Kohanim). In Judaeo-Arabic, with the address in both Judaeo-Arabic and Arabic script. Dating: Probably early 13th century. Reporting the arrival of two Venetian ships with wood, the anticipated arrival of a Venetian ship with no merchandise but with an ambassador (? rasūl), and a ship from Trapani (אטראבנש) with a Jewish proselyte. Some personal requests. (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)
Address, accompanying a letter or a shipment, from Fusṭāṭ to Jerusalem into the hands of Naṣrullah Bashshāʿ (?). Dating: Late, probably Mamluk-era. (Information in part from CUDL)

Recto: Budget of expenses for food on the two days of ʿUnṣura (Shavuot). 

Verso is in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. It may be related. Mentions Friday in the header. Names include Abū Naṣr b. Abū l-Khayr; Mufaḍḍal; Mūsā; Abū l-Majd al-ʿArīf; Abū l-Ḥasan b. Makārim; Sitt Ghazāl; Sulaymān; Abū l-Khayr; "mawlāy."

(Information in part from Goitein's index card.)
Accounts with list of names and Coptic numerals. Rudimentary hand. Mentions names such as ʿAlwān; Abū l-Surūr; ʿAbd al-Kāfī. (Information in part from CUDL)
Small fragment of a legal document, probably.
Letter mentioning Fusṭāṭ. (Information from CUDL.) Excerpts: אדנת לך בתסלימה . . . קד אבדת(?) עליה . . . פי מצר גיר . . . עליה מא ינזל . . . . ביתך הו ביתי
Maimonides, Mishne Tora, Hilkhot Tefilla u-Nesiʾat Kappayim 14:7-15:12; Hilkhot Tefillin u-Mezuza 1:1-10 with sporadic Persian (not Arabic) supralinear glosses. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Ownership note: Naḥum b. Yosef.
Letter mentioning Abū l-Barakāt and Jerusalem. (Information in part from CUDL)
Booklist

Fol. 2v: Legal document in Arabic script. Abū ʿAlī Ḥasan b. Khalaf, a Jew from Tyre, renounces all of his monetary claims against Isḥaq b. Sahl b. Bishr b. Nāḥūm and Abū Naṣr. Dating: 12th century CE. Fol. 1r: Arabic document of lease (needs further examination). On fols. 1v–2r and margins, there is a medical text dealing with parts of the human body. (Information from Khan and CUDL; see also Goitein's index card.)

Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Mentions al-muʿallim Ṣāliḥ; the cantor al-Mesos (المسوس الحزان); Hārūn ʿAbd al-Qawiyy; al-ʿAjamī; "In Cairo"; al-Baṣīr(?); Abū l-Ḥasan al-Mubayyiḍ; mentions flax; Ismāʿīl al-Ghazalī the acquaintance of ʿAbd al-Bāqī;Ibrāhīm the brother of ʿAbd al-Qawiyy; ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Ḥaffār; ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz "in his dwellling in Zuqāq al-Ruqyānī(?)."
Very little text remains to identify, possibly accounts. (Information from CUDL)

A leaf from the court register, with five different entries, all signed by Yiṣḥaq b. Shemu'el, all explicitly dated between Shevat and Iyyar 1410 Sel. (1099 CE).

Recto:
Righthand side: Nissim commits to pay alimonies for his son, for the period from the signing of this document, Monday Nissan 3rd 1410 Sel. (28.3.1099 CE), to the feast of Shavu'ot.
Signed by Yiṣḥaq b. Shemu'el.
Recto: Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Verso: Undeciphered text in Arabic script.

Possibly the last page of a copy of a decree (à la T-S Ar.40.37). Opens with a conditional clause (wa-lammā lam yuʾkhadh(?) al-amr...) and a statement that something must only be done after [...] from the dīwān (...illā baʿd [...] min al-dīwān al-saʿīd bi-l-[...] ḥarasa Allāh sultānahū...). There is then a reference to a noble rescript/decree (al-tawqīʿ al-karīm), an inshallāh, and a date (54[.] AH = 1145–54 CE). At the bottom: fa-wuqqiʿa.... On verso, there is a related text written in a hastier hand and occupying only four lines. Needs further examination.
Table of contents for a volume of responsa, including one about a marital problem of people in Toledo.

List possibly drawn up by a traveler to Constantinople giving the names and titles of six benefactors of his in the city, as well as the phrase 'the entire body of the congregation, may they be blessed', presumably used when praying for them in public so that no one would be forgotten. The names: Eliyya b. Shabbetay ha-Rav; the two brothers Eliyya b. Shabbetay ha-Rofeʾ ha-Sofer and his brother Yehuda; ʿOvadya ha-Ṣoref; and Yosef and his brother. (Information from Mediterranean Society, V, pp. 36, 515)

Legal document. Bū l-Majd b. Thābit, known as Meir b. Yakhin, appoints his brother Hilāl/Hillel as his attorney for all his claims and in particular those resulting from the estate of his deceased wife Sitt al-Dār bt. Bū l-Faḍl. Information from Goitein’s index card.
Placeholder [ASE]

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic, with the address in Arabic script. Addressed to Abū Ṭāhir Barakāt b. ʿAlī al-Baghdādī. The layout is somewhat unusual. It opens with blessings and longing and mentions the passing of time (not a person named Mar al-Zamān). Mentions a woman who has died (raḍiya Allāh ʿanhā). Mentions Abū l-Faḍl R. Maṣliaḥ. The last words in the upper margin are 'they have taken the money/property.' In addition to the address, verso contains the remains of an earlier letter or letter draft addressed to a woman. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Recto: responsa in the hand of Yosef b. Yaʿaqov Rosh ha-Seder. Verso: Judaeo-Arabic poem and dirge also written by Yosef. (Information from CUDL)
Bifolio of commercial accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: 11th or 12th century. Many details preserved but difficult to read. Needs further examination.
Top part of a ketubba. Dated: Thursday, 25 Adar 1770 Seleucid = 1 March 1459 CE. Location: Cairo. Two lines of the reshut formula are preserved. AA
Bifolium from a halakhic treatise. Likely in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Netanʾel.

Account of the qodesh, ca. June 1201. A relatively ample list of revenue and expenditures. The first part contains details of revenue from 17 compounds, inclusive of the dakakin (shops) and the funduq. These are shown to comprise 54 apartments and tenants. Out of these 54, ten are mentioned as unoccupied. The relatively large number of vacant apartments may indicate the beginning of the terrible famine period of A.H. 597 when whole neighborhoods and villages were deserted. (Information from Gil, Documents, pp. 378 #101.) In the hand of the court clerk Yosef b. Shemuel b. Saʿadya ha-Levi (ca. 1

Two lines of a state document probably, based on format. Very large. But might also something poetical, referring to love: ḥālī yattaṣilhā l-hawā wa-l-maḥabba wa-ʿindahumā tasquṭ al-munāẓara.... Reused on verso for Hebrew literary text.
Marriage contract (ketubba) concerning Badriyya,"who is single," the daughter of ʿAllūn. (Friedman, Jewish Marriage, vol. 2, 243-9) EMS
Very faded Arabic legal document - needs examination. Reused on verso for a piyyuṭ of Yiṣhaq ibn Ghiyath.
Business accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and eastern Arabic numerals. Dating: likely 18th or 19th century. Large and neatly written. Each column is headed by a name.

Official-looking document in Arabic script. Needs examination. 

Reused for pen trials in Judaeo-Arabic and jottings in Hebrew, and on recto for liturgical text in Hebrew. (Information in part from CUDL)
Account or calculations of some kind in Hebrew script.

Letter in which a man complains about a conflict over a power of attorney and a deposit. The sender of the letter held the opinion that he had not done his opponent any harm but the latter had accused him in public of the opposite, threatening to bring this and other matters to the attention of the government.
Magical adjuration (אשבעית . . . .). Formulary, based on the פל בר פל in l. 2.
Fragment from a letter in a 12th-century hand, which continues into the right-hand margin and closes with greetings for the high holiday. (Information from CUDL; see also Goitein's index card.)
Note/order addressed to Abū l-Faraj al-Kohen. In Judaeo-Arabic. Instructing him to collect four dirhams from the bearer, the 'boy' (ṣabiyy) of the sender. The note was left incomplete.

Minute fragment written by Halfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–38 CE). On recto Abū l-Faḍl is mentioned but there is too little text to contextualize. On verso probably a list of contributions to the poor. The widow of the Cretan (al-Iqrīṭishī) and Umm מנידו (a Greek name?) are each given 2 (dirhams?). AA/ASE

The end of a ketubba with a dowry list, referring to either Natan or Yonatan (or simply החתן). The list has been reused for writing practice, with many of the words repeated between the lines in a different hand. Dating: 12th or 13th century. (Information in part from CUDL)
Legal document. Small fragment. Involves someone named Efrayim, a woman, and al-Sammanūdī; also involves a debt and a document that was lost.

Letter of condolence from a woman (name unknown) to Ṣedaqa b. Ṣemaḥ, the son of her late brother. Opens with four lines of biblical verses in Hebrew commonly referred to as צידוק הדין, then continues in Judaeo-Arabic. The deceased seems to be female family member named ʿAzīza, who left orphaned girls behind (ll. 10–11). The sender says that the pain of her bereavement is equal to the pain that she experienced when her brother (Ṣedaqa's father) died (ll. 5–6). She invokes the trope that it is best not to grieve for too long, "because it does no good, all I have gained from sorrow and weeping is
Coptic mathematical table. Mostly fractions, including one section in a ruled tabular format.
Late account in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions the terms Dīwānī; muʿāmala; Qurayshī(?).
Fragment of a letter mentioning [...] b. ʿAbd al-Karīm. Dating: probably Mamluk-era. (Information in part from CUDL)
Order of payment.

Accounts in Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. Late. One side: "What I received from Yaʿaqov b. Khalīfa," then sums in sultanis, jadids, קורון, and ibrahimis. Of the various types of coinage listed, the reference to "ibrahimis" helps date this fragment as post-1520 CE, because this term likely denotes coinage minted according to standards of Avraham Castro's tenure as the overseer of the Ottoman mint in Cairo (post-1520-1524 CE). The other side: "What I paid R. Moshe."
Accounts.

tags: lost archive, Petition, Arabic script, DIMME
desc: Petition, draft, from an ex-government servant asking for work, presumably from a government official. From the period of the Fatimid caliph al-Ḥākim (996–1021) or possibly earlier. Recto, from later reuse: tax receipt in the hand of Mikhaʾil b. ʿAbd al-Masīḥ (see separate entry).
Recto: Letter of appeal for assistance in Hebrew. Related to the lepers of Tiberias? Describing grief and weeping and distress in vivid phrases.

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: perhaps 15th or 16th century. The sender is probably in Istanbul (r10); also mentions Antalya and two other locations in the next line. The letter is long and well-preserved, discussing numerous family and business matters. Commodities (all on verso) include lemon balm (taranjabīl), lapis lazuli (lāzuward), carum (aṭrīlān), dried okra (bāmya nāshifa), something whose price is "like that of pearl from Bā[...]," musk, ambergris. Needs further examination.
Hebrew literary text. In the margin of verso there are several cryptic words in Arabic script. Does not seem to be documentary. Needs examination.

Court record; concerned with legal issues between ʿUlla b. Joseph, the agent of Saʿd, and Maṣliaḥ b. Meshullam; signed by the witnesses Isaac, Abraham b. Shemaʿya and Shelomo b. Ṣedaqa (?). (Information from CUDL)
Letter addressed to a certain Shemuel. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Mamluk or early Ottoman era. Mentions the shop of the bāshā and פלוס דיואן אלקטר. Needs further examination.
Formulary for drawing up marriage documents. In Hebrew with some Ladino words (contante, joyas, mandiles). Location: Fustat/Cairo. Dating: Late. Currency: mithqāl/mathāqīl.
Business accounts in both Arabic and Judaeo-Arabic. Hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Very large. Dating: 11th or 12th century. Some names such as Manṣūr al-Farrāsh. AA/ASE
Small fragment with Hebrew script.
Small fragment with a few words in Hebrew, one of which is the name Shemarya.

Verso: Marriage contract dated 1050, between Saadya b. Maymun and Ḥasana bat Levi, mentioning 5 dinars that will be given at the time of the wedding and 20 dinars deferred. (Information from Mediterranean Society, III, p. 398) Recto: various texts, including a formula for a bill of divorce, and a Hebrew poem.
Beginning of a letter, mentioning the arrival of the addressee’s letter. Written on the 12th of Tishri. (Information from CUDL)

Fragment of a decree, part of one line of text barely visible on verso at right. 23 cm across, so it may have been split in half (Fatimid decrees were generally 40–45 cm across). (Information from MR).

Deathbed will of a rich woman, made during the absence of her husband. Location: Fustat. Dated: Wednesday, 26 Iyyar 1454 Seleucid, which is 13 April 1143 CE, under the reshut of Shemuel b. Ḥananya. Testator: Sitt al-Ahl bt. Abū l-Munā al-ʿAṭṭār al-Iskandarānī, the wife of Abū Naṣr al-Ḥalabī al-Tājir. Witnesses: Yosef b. Thābit ha-Levi; Shelomo b. Natan he-Ḥaver. "This remarkable deathbed declaration, on the one hand, shows the cosmopolitan character of Fustat: the daughter of a druggist called 'the Alexandrian' was married there to a merchant 'from Aleppo.' On the other hand, it betrays an ext

Letter from Shabbetay b. Avraham the judge of Minya Zifta to Yehuda b. Elʿazar ha-Kohen. Complaining that Abū l-Makārim b. Abū l-Dhamm (this is probably an insult rather than an actual name), an outsider from Cairo, had opened with two partners a store of medical potions, thereby doing harm to the Jews. (Information in part from Mediterranean Society, II, pp. 48, 67, 68, 533)

Verso: Mercantile account, different from recto, and seems to be in a different hand. There are two sections at 180 degrees to each other. Itemizing the expenses for shipping pepper and flax via Rosetta (Rashīd). Mentions bribes (barṭīl) costs for the ship, and the son of Nahray.

Recto: Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating; 11th century. Seems to be a list of debts (duyūn). The sums are quite large:

Letter drafts from a certain Shelomo. Rudimentary handwriting. On recto he states that he is unable to come because his father is sick. The draft on verso is addressed to Avraham ha-Sar Ner ha-Maʿaravi (probably Avraham Maimonides). In the margin he mentions "my brother and lord Abū l-Ṭāhir." (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)

tags: Illness, illness letter 969-1517, illness: fever, al-Mahdiyya, 11th c, epidemic, epidemic: wakham
desc: Letter from Mūsā b. Yiṣḥaq b. Nissim, in al-Mahdiyya, to Ismāʿīl b. Barhūn al-Tāhartī. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: ca. 1030. The writer is looking forward to the addressee's intended visit to al-Mahdiyya. He describes the situation in the Maghreb, and he mentions silk business and a large transfer of money to a yeshiva. "In a letter sent from Fustat to Qayrawan, Tunisia, we read this: 'A wakham like this I have not seen since I have come to Fustat. I was ill for a full four months with fever and fits of cold, which attacked me day and night. But God, for the sake of his name, not because of my m

State document, in Arabic script. Mentions an iqṭāʿ and kharāj. Dating: most likely Ayyubid due to the mention of "ṭawāshī", most probably meaning a military faction in the Ayyubid times, disintegrated by the Mamlūks, as per al-Qalqashandī. The scribe wrote with a nicked nib (which may facilitate finding a join). Needs examination for content. There is a Hebrew dirge on the verso.

IB VII, 34. Text of the oath that Bū ʿImrān must swear to his brother Abū l-Maʿānī concerning his mercantile activities, the price of a house, and the payment of the capitation tax during the time when Abū l-Maʿānī was absent (in Yemen or India). In the hand of Shelomo b. Eliyyahu. On verso there are also entries about the sale or exchange of books, perhaps in the hand of Shelomo b. Eliyyahu. Information from Goitein's attached notes.
Minute fragment, only few words preserved including אדוננו which might be from a letter or legal deed.
Booklist in Judaeo-Arabic. Information from Baker/Polliack catalog. Needs examination.

Note in the hand of Shelomo b. Eliyyahu. In Judaeo-Arabic. Stating that the ḥerem stam will be issued by the Nagid in the synagogues for the benefit of the children and heirs of Hilāl the Alexandrian, whose will was not taken down in sufficiently clear form. People obviously owed him money. Information from Goitein's note card.
Fol. 1: Halakhic discussion regarding the proper time for prayer.
Chaotic Arabic text, possibly documentary.

Verso: list of household expenses in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals, mentioning types of oil, soap, camphor, and green lemon; payments to a laborer; and  a visit to the bathhouse. For other lists of this type see Med. Soc IV, pp. 230–34.

tags: personal, ib-partial translation-heb, ib-untranslated-eng, illness letter 969-1517, Illness: treatment, Illness, illness: rich description, illness: hysteria, midwives, India Book, Illness: women's, IB4, late Alexandria
desc:
IB IV, 69 (ח79). Letter from ʿAmram b. Yiṣḥaq, in Alexandria, to Ḥalfon b. Netanel ha-Levi, in Fustat. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Middle of Adar 1451 Seleucid = February 1141 CE. 

The letter deals with the illness of ʿAmram's wife (evidently a family member of Ḥalfon's) and the way she was treated. She had been suffering lethargy, palpitations, and fainting spells for over a year and a half. She was treated for “the obstruction of the heart (inqifāl al-qalb) mentioned by al-Rāzī in the Manṣūrī,” but the medicine only made matters worse. Midwives were summoned to treat her for "the illness of

Fragment from the bottom of a legal document. Written and signed by Hillel b. ʿEli (fl. 1066–1108 CE). Also signed by Yiṣḥaq b. Shemuel and Avraham b. Sh[emaʿya?]. Involves a certain Avraham and the term ḍamān.
Annotations in Ladino in the margin of a printed work. Significance unclear.

Letter in which an ophthalmologist named Moshe blames his assistant who was also his relative for having left without giving him details about the various medications in the dispensary and chastises him and exhorts him to return to work. At one point he cites what must have been a proverbial expression, "which is higher in the head, the eyes or the molars?" This is followed by "return to God, and leave off folly. . . You have burnt my heart with your distance. . . ." He has sent some collyria along with the letter and wishes to know what they are. He also instructs the addressee to study the t

tags: epidemic: fever, Late JA, illness: fever, Hebron, epidemic, Illness
desc: Letter probably sent from Palestine to Egypt. In Judaeo-Arabic and Hebrew. Dating: ca. 13th–15th century (paleographic dating). There are two folios, which probably originally joined, but it's not clear precisely how. On the first page, the writer reports that "not only them, but the Alexandrians (ahl al-thaghr) who remained in Hebron "all fell sick with this fever" It is difficult to make out the subject of the remainder of the letter. Needs further examination.

Account of a Parnas ca. 1200. Upper part of a leaf in very deteriorated condition. It contains notes made by a parnas, recording the collection of sums for repairs in some houses of the qodesh. The verso contains several items of eexpenditures for an unnamed Nasi. (Information from Gil, Documents, pp. 392 #105)

Version of the letter in: Mosseri VII 155. Fragment of a letter from Yosef b. Berekhya, probably to Yosef b. Ya’aqov b. Awkal, Fustat. Around 1020. Another version of the letter was sent earlier through the sea and this letter was sent on the land. Both letters are very similar but not identical. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 2, #152) VMR
Letter from Shelomo b. Yehuda to Avraham Ha-Kohen, Sar Ha-Eda b. Yiṣḥaq. Dating: ca. 1025–1051 CE based on the years when Shelomo b. Yehuda served as Gaʾon.

Letter from Shelomo b. Yehuda to Efrayim b. Shemarya. Dating: probably summer 1029 CE (per Gil) and ca. 1025–1051 CE, based on the years when Shelomo b. Yehuda served as Gaʾon. Concerns, among other things, Shelomo b. Yehuda's traveling to Egypt to excommunicate followers of the Iraqi rite for their methods of butchering animals (Rustow, Heresy, p. 174).
Letter draft from Shelomo b. Eliyyahu to a woman (al-sitt al-rayyisa al-ʿazīza). In Judaeo-Arabic. Written in his worst handwriting.

Verso (secondary use): Complete letter in Hebrew prefaced by two biblical quotations (Psalms 120:1; 130:1). The writer is commiserating with the addressee’s disgrace, likely a bereavement: יסמו עינים שיראו קלונך ויחרשו אזנים שישמעו מקצת כלמתך, but puts his faith in divine justice, אבל נקבל דין השם. It is signed by ‘the insulted servant Yosef’ (העבד הנעלב יוסף). 

Recto (original use): Unidentified text in Arabic script. Might be medical or a prescription (seems to mention quantities and materia medica). (Information in part from CUDL)
IB V, 39c (previously V, 39b). An Abū Zikrī Kohen cheque. Khalīl is to give the bearer one raṭl of linseed oil.

tags: Abu Sahl Levi, personal, Moshe b. Levi
desc: Recto: Letter in the handwriting of Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi, probably from Qalyub to his father in Fustat, consisting almost in its entirely of good wishes for Tabernacles. He mentions that the turban (raddah) arrived. He mentions the wife of his paternal uncle, but the context is ambiguous. He then admits that he has no money even to buy bread, but all will end well. (Information from Mediterranean Society, V, pp. 87, 351.) Verso: Either the response or the initial letter, probably from Levi (Abu Sahl) to his son Moshe. Everyone in the family is well. The addressee's brother Abu l-Ḥasan is doin

Verso (original use): Deed of lease. In Arabic script. Fragment (upper right corner). The basmala and the beginnings of five lines are preserved. The lessee is Ibrāhīm b. Khalaf al-[...]. Reference is made to the bureau of the mosques (Dīwān al-Jawāmiʿ wa-l-Masājid) and to New Cairo (al-Qāhira al-Maḥrūsa). Dating: Mentions Dhū l-Qaʿda 525 AH = September/October 1131 CE.
